body.question: Euclid and Ptolemy thought sight works by the eye sending out rays. What did Ibn al-Haytham argue around 1030?
options: Eyes send out rays, but only in daylight
Every point of a lit object sends light along every straight line, and the eye receives it
Sight is a gift that cannot be explained
body.reveal: In his Book of Optics (written between 1028 and 1038) Ibn al-Haytham described objects as sending light and colour along every straight line from each point. He is credited as an early proponent of the idea that a hypothesis must be supported by experiments, about five centuries before Renaissance scientists.

probes.question: What did Ibn al-Haytham say a hypothesis needs?
True or false: Euclid and Ptolemy believed that sight works by the eye emitting rays of light.
